episode.title: Ep. 186 — A conversation with Lieutenant General Sami Sadat

persons.name: Sami Sadat
persons.role: Guest; former deputy commander Afghan Ground Forces, commander 209th Shaheen Corps (Balkh) and 215th Maiwand Corps (Helmand, 2020-21), briefly deputy chief of staff ANA; now leader of the Afghanistan United Front

mentions.quote: Sami served as the deputy commander of the Afghan Ground Forces, the commander of the 209th Shaheen Corps in Balkh province, the commander of the 215th Maiwand Corps in Helmand... deputy chief of staff of the Afghan National Army
I had a tough job of keeping my hands on my two cities, the city of Lashkar Gah, also the province of Nimroz.
I testified alongside Sami for the House Foreign Affairs Committee on the withdrawal from Afghanistan.

persons.name: Will Selber
persons.role: Guest co-host; retired Middle East Foreign Area Officer, military affairs fellow at The Bulwark; served at US Embassy Kabul 2020-21

mentions.quote: Today's co-host is my friend and colleague, Will Selber.

persons.name: Ashraf Ghani
persons.role: Former President of Afghanistan (2014-2021); refused Taliban deal without a principal agreement; described by Sadat as a poor wartime leader, a Democrat in the US for 26 years

mentions.quote: others, including President Ashraf Ghani, wouldn't accept it. Obviously, he wanted some kind of a principal agreement
Ghani was not the right leader for Afghanistan and most definitely not the right leader as a wartime leader.
President Ghani was a registered Democrat for 26 years in the United States.

persons.name: Hamid Karzai
persons.role: Former President of Afghanistan (2001-2014); selected at Bonn 2001 after Khalilzad rejected Sattar Sirat

mentions.quote: Neither was President Karzai as a wartime leader. I think President Karzai did a wonderful job of uniting the nation
The next day elected Hamid Karzai as a president.

persons.name: Burhanuddin Rabbani
persons.role: Former President of Afghanistan and Jamiat-e Islami leader who, per Sadat, led the anti-Soviet and anti-Taliban resistance politically; religious leader; issued national pardon incl. Taliban in 2001

mentions.quote: Professor Rabbani was the president, recognized globally who led the resistance, and Ahmad Shah Massoud was the military leader.
once he captured Kabul, then he announced a pardon, a national pardon for everybody, including the Taliban.

persons.name: Ahmad Shah Massoud
persons.role: Military leader of the anti-Taliban resistance under Rabbani

mentions.quote: A lot of people in the West think Ahmad Shah Massoud led the resistance, but that's not true... Ahmad Shah Massoud was the military leader.

persons.name: Atta Mohammad Noor
persons.role: Northern Alliance commander under Rabbani

mentions.quote: like Atta Muhammad Noor, Ismail Khan, Hajji Qadir, Hazrat Ali, these are capable individuals. Marshal Fahim, and all of them worked for Professor Rabbani.

persons.name: Ismail Khan
persons.role: Northern Alliance commander under Rabbani

mentions.quote: Atta Muhammad Noor, Ismail Khan, Hajji Qadir, Hazrat Ali

persons.name: Abdul Qadir
persons.role: Northern Alliance / eastern commander under Rabbani

mentions.quote: Ismail Khan, Hajji Qadir, Hazrat Ali

persons.name: Hazrat Ali
persons.role: Resistance commander under Rabbani

mentions.quote: Hajji Qadir, Hazrat Ali, these are capable individuals

persons.name: Mohammed Fahim
persons.role: Resistance commander under Rabbani

mentions.quote: Marshal Fahim, and all of them worked for Professor Rabbani

persons.name: Zalmay Khalilzad
persons.role: US envoy at Bonn 2001 who, per Sadat, rejected Sattar Sirat and engineered Karzai's selection

mentions.quote: In Bonn in 2001, then again, Khalilzad showed up, and a bunch of CIA and others bribed Yunus Qanuni

persons.name: Yunus Qanuni
persons.role: Represented the Rabbani government at Bonn 2001; per Sadat was bribed to accept a new leader

mentions.quote: a bunch of CIA and others bribed Yunus Qanuni, who was representing the government of Afghanistan to agree to a new leader

persons.name: Mohammed Zahir Shah
persons.role: Last King of Afghanistan; in Rome in 2001; died 2006; Sadat's preferred constitutional-monarch option

mentions.quote: The other strong contender was late King Zahir Shah, His Majesty, was still alive. He was in Rome... he died in 2006.

persons.name: Abdul Sattar Sirat
persons.role: Former chief of staff to King Zahir Shah; chosen as interim leader by Bonn delegates before Khalilzad's intervention

mentions.quote: Then they chose Sattar Sirat, who was also the chief of staff for his majesty, the king... And then Khalilzad goes like, oh, no, you know, this is the wrong choice.

persons.name: Barack Obama
persons.role: Former US President; Doha office established and Guantanamo detainees released under him per Sadat

mentions.quote: the foundation of the whole problem began during President Obama... the Doha office was established during President Obama. The Guantanamo detainees were released under his orders

persons.name: Joe Biden
persons.role: US President; withdrawal from Afghanistan described by Sadat as bin Laden's greatest win

mentions.quote: The biggest win that bin Laden could never dream of was delivered by President Biden from the White House by saying that we're leaving Afghanistan

persons.name: Stanley McChrystal
persons.role: US commander in Afghanistan removed in 2010 after remarks about Biden

mentions.quote: it was President Biden who took out the best American field commander, General McChrystal

persons.name: Richard Holbrooke
persons.role: Obama-era envoy who per Sadat sought to unseat Karzai in 2009

mentions.quote: Then Richard Holbrooke and a couple of others got together. They wanted to set President Karzai down and defeat him in the elections in 2009

persons.name: Laurie Bristow
persons.role: Last UK ambassador to Afghanistan; author of 'Kabul: Final Call'

mentions.quote: the UK ambassador to Afghanistan, the last ambassador, Laurie Bristow, he wrote a book... Kabul final call

persons.name: Mullah Dadullah
persons.role: Taliban commander whose return from Helmand ignited the 2006 Taliban resurgence

mentions.quote: the Taliban resurgence in 2006 has actually emerged back from Helmand with Mullah Dadullah coming back and igniting the resurgence

persons.name: Hibatullah Akhundzada
persons.role: Taliban emir (Amir al-Muminin) to whom al-Qaeda and its branches pledge allegiance

mentions.quote: consecutive Al-Qaeda leaders always pledged their allegiance to Mullah Haibatullah... al-Qaeda in the Maghreb, al-Qaeda in Indian subcontinent, al-Qaeda in Arabian Peninsula... They pledge their allegiance to Mullah Hibatullah Akhundzada, the leader of the Taliban

persons.name: Mullah Omar
persons.role: Founding Taliban emir; bin Laden pledged allegiance to him

mentions.quote: bin Laden has pledged his allegiance to Mullah Omar

persons.name: Osama bin Laden
persons.role: Founder of al-Qaeda; pledged allegiance to Mullah Omar

mentions.quote: bin Laden has pledged his allegiance to Mullah Omar
on the eve of 9-11, there was a couple of Al-Qaeda lieutenants with bin Laden and Afghanistan, and they had about probably 3,000 followers

persons.name: Ayman al-Zawahiri
persons.role: Former al-Qaeda emir; per Sadat he and his deputies thought they would not survive the US presence

mentions.quote: Many of them, including Zawahiri and his deputies, thought they would never survive.

persons.name: Saif al-Adel
persons.role: Head of al-Qaeda global operations; per Sadat met IRGC and Taliban representatives after the fall of Kabul to unite Sunni and Shia militant groups against the US

mentions.quote: Saif al-Adel, the head of the global operation for al-Qaeda, then sat with the IRGC leaders, and they, and the Taliban representative as well. They said we have to leave our differences behind and we have to unite all the Sunni Mujahideen groups

persons.name: Abu Muhammad al-Jolani
persons.role: Syrian jihadist leader (Sadat describes him as leader of Hurras al-Din) allegedly called to Afghanistan and told to unite Shia and Sunni militants in Syria

mentions.quote: There's a guy whose name is Abu Muhammad al-Jolani. He was called into Afghanistan. He's in Syria. He was the leader of Hurras al-Din. And then he was told that your job is to unite the Shia and the Sunni militants in Syria.

persons.name: Sirajuddin Haqqani
persons.role: Taliban interior minister and Haqqani Network leader; traveled to UAE and Hajj June 2024; per Sadat ordered a Haqqani commander (Sanaullah Ghafari) to join ISKP so ISKP could keep attacking Americans

mentions.quote: allowing men like Sirajuddin Haqqani to leave Afghanistan, travel to UAE, shake hands with their president, and then he goes on the Hajj
This guy is literally the definition of a human butcher... his men directed thousands of suicide attacks
Sanaullah Ghafari, the current leader of ISKP was a Haqqani commander who turned into ISIS with direct orders from Sirajuddin Haqqani.
Haqqani achieved with his brother, his father never could.

persons.name: Anas Haqqani
persons.role: Brother of Sirajuddin Haqqani; accompanied him on the June 2024 trip

mentions.quote: Haqqani achieved with his brother, his father never could.

persons.name: Jalaluddin Haqqani
persons.role: Father of Sirajuddin Haqqani; Haqqani Network founder

mentions.quote: Haqqani achieved with his brother, his father never could.

persons.name: Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan
persons.role: UAE President who received Sirajuddin Haqqani (June 2024)

mentions.quote: I was very annoyed with Sheikh Muhammad bin Zayed meeting him as well.

persons.name: Sanaullah Ghafari
persons.role: Current leader of ISKP; per Sadat a former Haqqani commander who switched to ISIS on Sirajuddin Haqqani's orders

mentions.quote: Sanaullah Ghafari, the current leader of ISKP was a Haqqani commander who turned into ISIS with direct orders from Sirajuddin Haqqani.
Not to say that Sanaullah is listening to everything that Sirajuddin says today. He's now a powerful man

persons.name: Hafiz Saeed Khan
persons.role: Former TTP/Taliban commander from Orakzai who was the first to pledge allegiance to ISKP (named by Sadat only as 'the Orakzai'; identification inferred)

mentions.quote: The first person that pledged allegiance to ISKP was a Taliban commander, you know, the Orakzai, who went on and pledged his allegiance to ISKP.

persons.name: Tariq al-Bangali
persons.role: Senior al-Qaeda member leading the Shorabak (Kandahar) training camp raided in Oct 2015

mentions.quote: there was a senior al-Qaeda member leading it, Tariq al-Bangali. And there were Indians, Bengalis, Arabs, Pakistanis

persons.name: Abu Musab al-Zarqawi

mentions.quote: 20 maybe group commanders to include Zawahiri, al-Baghdadi, Abu Musab al-Zarqawi

persons.name: Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi
persons.role: Later Islamic State leader, cited by Sadat as example of a commander type

mentions.quote: Zawahiri, Al-Baghdadi, Abu Musab al-Zarqawi, and some of the others that became well-known leaders

persons.name: David Kilcullen
persons.role: Strategy advisor to Sadat's Afghanistan United Front

mentions.quote: David Kilcullen, who is my strategy advisor

persons.name: Sarah Adams

mentions.quote: I continue to say to you, to Will, to others, to Sarah Adams, like, keep doing this.

organizations.name: al-Qaeda
organizations.notes: Sadat claims ~40,000 armed al-Qaeda members in Afghanistan (100,000+ with families), ~1,000 commanders; majority foreign (India, Pakistan, Libya, Somalia, Yemen, Middle East) with growing Afghan recruitment. Contrasts sharply with UN estimates.

organizations.name: Taliban
organizations.notes: Per Sadat: 85% of senior commanders from Helmand; supporters are Iran, Pakistan, US and China; uses al-Qaeda as deniable external arm; now fighting Pakistan and eroding ties with Iran.

organizations.name: Haqqani Network

organizations.name: ISKP

organizations.name: Islamic State
organizations.notes: Tactical, quick-results organization vs al-Qaeda's strategic approach per Sadat.

organizations.name: AQIS

events.description: Collapse of the Afghan republic; Sadat cites Doha deal, divided government, and halted US ammunition/technical support as the three causes.
Taliban mass assaults on Lashkar Gah 2020-21 with TTP, AQIS and Iranian fighters; up to seven car bombs a day; 175:1 claimed kill ratio.
Doha Agreement made without Afghan government consent; alleged secret clause halting US ammunition and technical support to the ANA (per Laurie Bristow's book).
Taliban resurgence ignited from Helmand with Mullah Dadullah's return.
Bonn conference: delegates chose Sattar Sirat, Khalilzad objected, Yunus Qanuni allegedly bribed, Hamid Karzai selected next day.
Rabbani, back in Kabul, announced a national pardon including the Taliban; many Taliban surrendered weapons before US raids reversed this.
Holbrooke and others sought to defeat Karzai in the 2009 election; Ghani eventually won in 2014.
General McChrystal removed after remarks about Biden.
CIA director estimate of 50-100 al-Qaeda in Afghanistan, maintained unchanged for six years.

US-Afghan raid on two al-Qaeda camps in Shorabak, Kandahar: ~150-200 fighters killed, media center, SIGINT intercept capability, Indians/Bengalis/Arabs/Pakistanis, led by Tariq al-Bangali; 'largest al-Qaeda camp since 9/11'.
Per Sadat, al-Qaeda and Houthis stopped fighting in Yemen after a Saif al-Adel–IRGC–Taliban understanding to unite Sunni and Shia militants against the US.
Sirajuddin Haqqani visits UAE, meets MBZ, then performs Hajj; Sadat calls it a recruitment video for hundreds of thousands.
Al-Qaeda attack on a force in Burkina Faso killed over 100 soldiers 'a week ago'.
FBI joint terrorism task force arrests eight Tajik nationals in the US with suspected ISIS ties, linked by hosts to the Moscow (Crocus) attack.
Moscow attack earlier in 2024 referenced in connection with Tajik ISIS recruits.
Sadat and Roggio testified before the House Foreign Affairs Committee on the Afghanistan withdrawal.
Afghanistan United Front reached an agreement with one neighboring country and is negotiating with another; next step a military commission and fundraising.
Taliban killed Iranian border guards on several occasions; Iran did not retaliate.

key_claims: Sadat: the Taliban–al-Qaeda bond is generational and religious — bin Laden pledged to Mullah Omar and every al-Qaeda leader and branch (AQIM, AQIS, AQAP) pledges to Hibatullah — reinforced by intermarriage and shared combat; the relationship is as close as UK–US or closer.

Sadat claims ~40,000 armed al-Qaeda fighters and ~1,000 commanders in Afghanistan today (100,000+ with families), far above UN figures, and says al-Qaeda is stronger than ever because of the Taliban comeback.

Sadat alleges a post-2021 Saif al-Adel–IRGC–Taliban understanding to unite Sunni and Shia militants against US bases, citing a halt in al-Qaeda–Houthi fighting since Dec 2021 and Hezbollah facilitation.
Sadat alleges ISKP leader Sanaullah Ghafari was a Haqqani commander sent to ISKP on Sirajuddin Haqqani's orders so attacks on Americans could continue after Doha.
Three causes of the 2021 collapse: the Doha deal made without the Afghan government, a divided Afghan political class, and the cut-off of US ammunition/technical support and contractors.
Helmand is the Taliban's center of gravity (85% of senior commanders), and Iran and Pakistan push fighters across its borders.
Sirajuddin Haqqani's UAE visit and Hajj are a global recruitment advertisement; Gulf rulers who think they can control the Taliban are wrong.
Hosts contradict Biden's 'mortal enemies' framing of Taliban–ISKP and oppose CT partnership with the Taliban.
Afghanistan United Front plans an Afghan-led military campaign against the Taliban with an agreement already reached with one neighboring state.
